facts.fact: The National Registration (Amendment) Act 2025 (assented 23 March 2025) requires the registrar to process personal data in accordance with the Data Protection Act, which it treats as an existing law.

The National Registration (Amendment) Act 2025 (No. 7), assented 23 March 2025, amends the existing National Registration Act (Cap. 01:02); the amendment starts on a date the Minister sets by Gazette order, not yet stated.
The 2025 amendment, not yet commenced, has the registrar assign a gender-neutral identity number to each person in the Unified Population Register and issue an identity card valid 10 years.

BWA.note: No enrolment count or share given.
Registration is at age 16 under the Act; no number at birth stated.
Nothing on who operates, maintains or owns the system.
No other register keyed on the identity number stated.
The Act provides for an ID card and number but does not say a system is issuing them.

facts.fact: The National Registration (Amendment) Act 2025 (No. 7), assented 23 March 2025, provides for a Unified Population Register of all citizens, dual citizens and non-citizen residents kept by the registrar; commencement is on ministerial notice.
